To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the BlaI repressor from Staphyloccocus aureus forms homodimers and that the dimer interacts with the DNA target of the mecA promoter-operator in an up-and down-arrangement, whereas the dimer of the MecI repressor from S. aureus interacts with the DNA of the blaZ promoter-operator in an in-line arrangement.
BlaI represses transcription of the blaZ gene encoding β-lacatamase in staphyloccoci.
BlaI and MecI repressors from S. aureus bind to the mec and the bla DNA promoter-operator regions, respectively, and the structures of Bla and Mec in complex with DNA have been determined.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure of the BlaR1 receptor and its interaction with BlaI. The receptor, a serine protease, is activated by binding β-lactam antibiotic.
the elucidation of the molecular basis of the regulation of antibiotic resistance in Staphylococcal bacteria.
the elucidation of the structure of BlaR1, BlaI, and their complexes with DNA and with BlaR1 and its complex with the inducer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
both BlaI and MecI bind to the same face of DNA and the same helix-turn-helices of the DNA double helix.
the crystal structure of the BlaR1 sensor protein in complex with the BlaI repressor has been solved.
the repressor proteins BlaI and MecI, in their free form or bound to DNA, are very similar in structure and in their mode of DNA binding.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have solved crystal structures of the BlaR1 and MecI proteins, which regulate the transcription of the mecA and blaZ genes in staphyloccoci, respectively, and have determined their complexes with DNA, which are responsible for the repression of the transcription of the genes.
BlaI and MecI have a common fold, bind the same DNA target, and may have a common mechanism of induction.
the BlaI repressor binds DNA as a dimer, with the DNA binding domain of the repressor contacting the DNA via the recognition helix α-3.
The main takeaway from our work is that
BlaI and MecI repressors bind DNA in a very similar manner.

BlaI is an example of a repressor that can bind to two different operator sequences with different specificities, and the crystal structures of Blas in complex with the two operators reveal the structural basis of this specificity.
BlaI and MecI are homologous proteins with similar structures, and they recognize the DNA target sequences in a very similar manner.
